# Employment Contract Templates Skill — Overview & Workflow

## Skill Purpose

This skill provides templates and patterns for creating **legally sound employment documentation**, including contracts, offer letters, and HR policies. Use it when drafting employment agreements, creating HR policies, or standardizing employment documentation.

> **IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER:** These templates are for informational purposes only and **do not constitute legal advice**. Always consult with qualified legal counsel before using any employment documents.

---

## When to Use This Skill

- Drafting employment contracts
- Creating offer letters
- Writing employee handbooks
- Developing HR policies
- Standardizing employment documentation
- Onboarding documentation

---

## Employment Document Types

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** | Initial job offer | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal agreement | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies & procedures | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality | Before access |
| **Non-Compete** | Competition restriction | Hire/Exit |

---

## Key Legal Considerations (Before Drafting)

```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

---

## Workflow: Creating an Offer Letter

The recommended workflow when using this skill to produce an offer letter:

### Step 1 — Determine Employment Classification
- Is this **at-will** or **contract** employment?
- **Full-time vs. part-time**?
- **Exempt vs. non-exempt** (overtime eligibility)?
- Confirm **jurisdiction-specific requirements** for the state/country where the employee will work.

### Step 2 — Use Template 1 (Offer Letter)

The skill provides a complete offer letter template structured as follows:

1. **Company letterhead & date**
2. **Candidate address block** (salutation)
3. **Position Details** — Title, Department, Reports To, Location, Start Date, Employment Type (Full-Time/Part-Time + Exempt/Non-Exempt)
4. **Compensation**
   - Base Salary (amount + pay frequency: bi-weekly/semi-monthly/monthly)
   - Bonus (percentage + performance criteria, or "Not applicable")
   - Equity (shares/options with vesting schedule, or "Not applicable")
5. **Benefits** — Health insurance effective date, 401(k) match, PTO days, paid holidays, other perks. Note: "Full details will be provided during onboarding."
6. **Contingencies** — Background check, right-to-work verification, execution of supporting documents (Confidentiality Agreement, Non-Compete where applicable, IP Assignment Agreement)
7. **At-Will Employment clause** — Crucial language stating employment may be terminated by either party at any time, with or without cause or notice; explicitly states the letter does not constitute a contract of employment for a specific period.
8. **Acceptance section** — Signature lines, offer deadline/expiration, return instructions.

**Placeholders to fill for your senior software engineer offer letter:** `[DATE]`, `[Candidate Name/Address]`, `[JOB TITLE]`, `[COMPANY NAME]`, `[Department]`, `[Manager Name/Title]`, `[Location]`, `[Start Date]`, `[Salary]`, `[Bonus %]`, `[Equity]`, `[Benefits dates/amounts]`, `[Offer expiry date]`, `[HR Contact]`, `[Hiring Manager Name/Title]`.

### Step 3 — Consider Adding a Formal Employment Agreement

In many cases (especially for senior roles), an offer letter is accompanied by a formal **Employment Agreement** (Template 2) covering:

- **§1 Employment** — Position, duties, best efforts, work location
- **§2 Term** — Employment period; at-will OR fixed-term
- **§3 Compensation** — Base salary, discretionary bonus, equity grant, benefits eligibility, expense reimbursement
- **§4 Confidentiality** — Definition of confidential info, non-disclosure obligations, return of materials, survival terms (trade secrets = indefinite; other info = 3 years)
- **§5 Intellectual Property** — Work product ownership, assignment to company, assistance requirements, prior inventions exhibit
- **§6 Non-Competition & Non-Solicitation** — ⚠️ *Note that enforceability varies by jurisdiction — consult local counsel.* Typically 12-month restricted periods for competition, customer solicitation, and employee solicitation
- **§7 Termination** — For cause / without cause / voluntary; severance provisions; survival of sections after termination
- **§8 General Provisions** — Entire agreement, amendments, governing law, dispute resolution, severability, notices, assignment, waiver
- **§9 Acknowledgments** — Employee confirms reading, had counsel opportunity, voluntary consent

### Step 4 — Verify Company Policies Align

Ensure the offer letter's benefits and PTO references align with your **Employee Handbook policy section** (Template 3), including:
- Equal Employment Opportunity statement
- Anti-harassment policy & reporting procedure
- Work hours/attendance expectations
- PTO accrual table (e.g., 15 days years 0–2, 20 days years 3–5, 25 days 6+)
- Sick leave allowance
- Paid holiday list
- Code of conduct

---

## Best Practices

### Do's
- **Consult legal counsel** — Employment law varies by jurisdiction
- **Keep copies signed** — Document all agreements
- **Update regularly** — Laws and policies change
- **Be clear and specific** — Avoid ambiguity
- **Train managers** — On policies and procedures

### Don'ts
- **Don't use generic templates** — Customize for your jurisdiction
- **Don't make promises** — That could create implied contracts
- **Don't discriminate** — In language or application
- **Don't forget at-will language** — Where applicable
- **Don't skip review** — Have legal counsel review all documents

---

## External Resources

- [SHRM Employment Templates](https://www.shrm.org/)
- [Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/)
- [EEOC Guidance](https://www.eeoc.gov/)
- State-specific labor departments

---

## Summary for Your Task

To create the **senior software engineer offer letter**, you will:

1. Use **Template 1** from the skill documentation (full markdown template above) as your base document.
2. Confirm the role's classification (presumably full-time, salaried/exempt, at-will).
3. Fill in all bracketed placeholders with the candidate and compensation details.
4. Attach the applicable contingency documents (Confidentiality Agreement, IP Assignment — both highly relevant for a senior engineering role).
5. If needed, pair it with a formal **Employment Agreement (Template 2)** covering IP assignment, confidentiality, and possibly non-compete clauses — but have legal counsel validate enforceability in your jurisdiction.
6. Ensure referenced benefits/PTO match your handbook policies.
7. Have legal counsel review before sending.
